 Find holiday gifts and community connections at Yakima Valley bazaars
 People shop around at the Holiday Bazaar at Harman Center Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025, in Yakima, Wash. Evan Abell / Yakima Herald-Republic ▲ 
 Knitted crafts sit on a table at the Holiday Bazaar at Harman Center Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025, in Yakima, Wash. Evan Abell / Yakima Herald-Republic ▲ 
 Cookies sit among other baked goods at the Lower Naches Women’s Club table at the Holiday Bazaar at Harman Center Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025, in Yakima, Wash. Evan Abell / Yakima Herald-Republic ▲ 
 SARA RAE SHIELDS
Yakima Herald-Republic 
 2 hrs ago 
 Holiday bazaar season is as much a tradition as decorating the Christmas tree or baking holiday cookies.
 Across the Yakima Valley, bazaars bring together local vendors selling handmade gifts, holiday decorations and other one-of-a-kind finds. But for many shoppers, the appeal goes beyond finding something to put under the tree.
 It’s also about community, tradition and reconnecting with familiar faces.
 Monique Stine, a retired kindergarten teacher who has organized bazaars at Holy Family Catholic Church since 2010, has seen those connections bring people back year after year.
 “It’s more of an event where you get together with friends,” she said. “It’s a social thing for us.”
 For some, that means running into old friends they haven’t seen in years. For others, it’s an annual outing with family or a chance to discover something new from a local vendor.
 Beyond the social aspect, bazaars offer something that online shopping can’t quite replicate, Stine said.
 Shoppers can see handmade items up close, talk with the people who made them and learn about the work that goes into each piece.
 “Instead of sitting at your desk by yourself looking at a screen to shop, you’re getting out and talking to people,” Stine said.
 And every purchase supports someone in the community, whether it’s a neighbor, a friend or a local maker.
 “Come out and support your neighbors,” Stine said. “It's the absolute best part of the season.”
 With so many bazaars taking place throughout the season, Stine suggested shoppers clip out the accompanying list, mark the ones they want to visit and plan a few holiday outings with friends or family.
 If your organization is hosting a holiday bazaar that's not listed here, email sshields@yakimaherald.com or use the Yakima Herald-Republic’s online calendar at www.yakimaherald.com/calendar .
 Here is a roundup of some of the holiday bazaars Explore found on social media:
 Nov. 6
 • Selah Kids Market, 5:30-7:30 p.m., Selah Civic Center, 216 S. First St., Selah. Arts, crafts, food, gifts and services.
 Nov. 6-7
 • Christmas Barn Sale, 9 a.m.-6 p.m., 1212 Cottonwood Canyon Road, Yakima. Christmas décor, gifts, handmade items and furniture. Free apple cider and cookies.
 Nov. 7
 • Winter Wonderland in Wiley, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Ahtanum Valley Elementary, 3006 S. Wiley Road, Yakima. Vendors and handmade goods.
 • Holly Jolly Christmas Bazaar, 8 a.m.-3 p.m., Our Lady of Lourdes Mel Allen Hall, 1111 W. Fremont Ave., Selah. Handcrafted items, Christmas decorations, gifts, dolls, toys, baked goods and candy. Silent auction, raffle at 3 p.m. Lunch, tamales and lumpia available for purchase.
 • Winter Bazaar, 9 a.m., West Valley Missionary Church, 11107 Wide Hollow Road, Yakima. Homemade baked goods, crafts and luncheon.
 • Holiday Bazaar, 8 a.m.-3 p.m., Harman Center, 101 N. 65th Ave. More than 60 vendors, raffles, coffee bar and bake sale. Breakfast $7 and lunch $6.
 • Winter Craft Bazaar, 8 a.m.-3 p.m., Crosspoint Church, 7803 Ahtanum Road. Unique crafts, holiday cheer.
 • Holy Redeemer Holiday Bazaar, 9 a.m.-4 p.m., Holy Redeemer Catholic Parish, 1707 S. Third Ave. Vendors with handcrafted, repurposed and retail items. Lunch and snack items available for purchase. Hourly raffles.
 • Holiday Market, 8 a.m.-2 p.m., West Valley Foursquare Church, 5802 Summitview Ave. More than 50 vendors with a variety of handmade goods, treats and unique finds.
 • Grandview High School Fall Bazaar, 9 a.m.-2 p.m., Grandview High School, 1601 W. Fifth St., Grandview. Handmade crafts, gifts, food and other unique items.
 • Goose & Beetle Christmas Market, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., 1361 Gore Road, Selah. Art, jewelry, baked goods, furniture, vintage finds, home decor, one-of-a-kind gifts and more. Donation of gloves and/or socks for gift basket drawing. 
 Nov. 7-8
 • Christmas on the Farm, 10 a.m.-3 p.m. Saturday; 11 a.m.-3 p.m. Sunday, French Canyon Farms, 120 Noye Road, Tieton. Photos with Santa, Frosty and Gingerbread Man both days. Food and drink. Christmas vendors. Other activities for a fee.
 Nov. 13-14
 • Christmas Barn Sale, 9 a.m.-6 p.m., 1212 Cottonwood Canyon Road, Yakima. Christmas décor, gifts, handmade items and furniture. Free apple cider and cookies.
 • Tree Top Holiday Bazaar, 5-8 p.m. Friday; 9 a.m.-3 p.m. Saturday, Selah Civic Center, 216 S. First St., Selah. Shop local, find unique gifts and seasonal magic.
 Nov. 14
 • Freedom Kits of Yakima Holiday Bazaar, 10 a.m.-3 p.m., 610 S. 96th Ave., Yakima.
 • Sip N Shop, 8 a.m.-whenever, Red Rooster Bar, 519 S. First St., Selah. Local vendors, handmade goods, home décor, jewelry and accessories, beauty, self-care, food and treats and more.
 • Yakima Covenant Church Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Yakima Covenant Church, 6015 Summitview Ave.
 • Holiday Bazaar, 10 a.m.-3 p.m., Filipino American Community Hall, 211 W. Second St., Wapato. Holiday crafts, baked goods, jewelry, pottery, art, beadwork, décor and more. Filipino cuisine (adobo, lumpia, pancit and rice), coffee, soda and water for sale.
 • Fall Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Central Lutheran Church, 1604 W. Yakima Ave.
 • Hope for the Nations Christmas Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Hope for the Nations Foursquare Church, 606 Washington Ave., Toppenish. Local vendors selling handmade crafts, baked goods, home décor, jewelry and accessories, art and more.
 • Homespun Crafters Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., West Valley Fire Station, 10000 Zier Road, Yakima. More than 40 local vendors selling handmade crafts and goodies. Lunch available for purchase.
 • Ellensburg Holiday Market, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Kittitas Valley Event Center, 901 E. Seventh Ave., Ellensburg. More than 50 local vendors. Pictures with Santa & Mrs. Claus, food trucks, coffee. In Teanaway and Umptanum halls. Free admission.
 • The Market at Meadowbrook, 10 a.m.-4 p.m., Meadowbrook Mall, 7200 W. Nob Hill Blvd. More than 50 local artisans, crafters and small businesses and more. Food stands.
 • Tinsel the Town preview night, 6-8 p.m., Flipper’s Antiques, 519 W. Yakima Ave. Annual opening of Christmas room. Sip, snack and shop and find vintage treasures.
 • Holiday Market, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., The Floral Station, 10120 U.S. Highway 12, Naches. Crafters in full holiday mode.
 • Holiday Market, 11 a.m.-3 p.m., Single Hill Brewing, 102 N. Naches Ave. Support local community members and makers. 
 Nov. 15
 • Tinsel the Town opening day, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., Flipper’s Antiques, 519 W. Yakima Ave. Annual Christmas room. Sip, snack and shop and find vintage treasures.
 Nov. 20
 • Exclusive Early Bird Sale Holy Family’s Holiday Bazaar, 6-8 p.m., Holy Family Catholic Church, 5315 Tieton Drive and 5508 W. Chestnut Ave. Shop before the crowds; Early access $5 wristbands required; buy at the door or in advance.
 Nov. 21
 • Wesley Craft Fair, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Wesley UMC of Yakima, 14 N. 48th Ave. Yakima. Soup, sandwich and pie lunch available for purchase, United Women of Faith booths, local artisans and vendors.
 • Naches Valley PTSA Holiday Bazaar, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., Naches Valley Middle School, 32 Schafer Ave., Naches. Local crafter, makers, small businesses and other vendors.
 • Holy Family’s Holiday Bazaar, 8 a.m.-3 p.m., Holy Family Catholic Church, 5315 Tieton Drive and 5508 W. Chestnut Ave. More than 100 vendors, food vendors and hourly raffles. Soup and sandwich luncheon. Free admission.
 • Holiday Pop & Shop, 11 a.m.-3 p.m., Klassy Stylz, 3904 Terrace Heights Drive, Suite D, Yakima. Local vendors and festive finds. Free and family friendly.
 • Hometown Holiday Bazaar, 8 a.m.-3 p.m., Best Western Plus The Inn at Horse Heaven, 259 Merlot Drive, Prosser. Crafts, candles and gifts. Check out the cowboy corner. 
 Nov. 28
 • Freedom Kits of Yakima Holiday Bazaar, 10 a.m.-3 p.m., 610 S. 96th Ave., Yakima.
 Dec. 3-5
 • Central Washington University’s annual Ware Fair, noon-6 p.m. Dec. 3; 10 a.m.-6 p.m. Dec. 4; 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Dec. 5, Central Washington University Student Union and Rec Center, 1007 N. Chestnut St., Ellensburg.
 Dec. 4-6
 • The Mighty Tieton Holiday Craft & Antique Bazaar, Tieton. Vendors located at The Mighty Tieton Warehouse, 608 Wisconsin Ave., as well as surrounding businesses. Find updates at www.mightytieton.com .
 Dec. 5
 • Christmas Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Eisenhower High School, 611 S. 44th Ave., Yakima. Pancakes served from 9-11 a.m. and photos with Santa from 10 a.m.-1 p.m.
 • The Market at Meadowbrook, 10 a.m.-4 p.m., Meadowbrook Mall, 7200 W. Nob Hill Blvd. More than 50 local artisans, crafters and small businesses and more. Food stands.
 • Christmas Bazaar, 9 a.m.-2 p.m., Fraternal Order of Eagles 289, 307 W. Chestnut Ave., Yakima. Handmade items, unique gifts, holiday décor, baked goods and more. Lunch for purchase 11 a.m.-1 p.m.
 • Highland Cheer Holiday Bazaar, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., Highland Middle & High School Commons, 17000 Summitview Road, Cowiche.
 • Holiday Market, 11 a.m.-3 p.m., Single Hill Brewing, 102 N. Naches Ave. Support local community members and makers. 
 Dec. 12
 • Holiday Artisan Market, 11 a.m.-5 p.m., Bosma Estate Winery, 1000 E. Houghton Road, Outlook. Local shopping, seasonal gift ideas, regional artisans, makers and handcrafted goods.
 • Zillah Middle School Holiday Bazaar, 9 a.m.-2 p.m., Zillah Middle School, 1301 Cutler Way, Zillah. Shop local vendors for the holiday season.
 • Selah High School Holiday Bazaar, 9 a.m.-1 p.m., Selah High School VPAC, 801 N. First St., Selah.
 Dec. 19
 • The Market at Meadowbrook, 10 a.m.-4 p.m., Meadowbrook Mall, 7200 W. Nob Hill Blvd. More than 50 local artisans, crafters and small businesses and more. Food stands.
